stemMd: A living plant cell placed in a concentrated sucrose solution develops a gap between its cell wall and plasma membrane. What directly causes this gap?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Active export of the entire cytoplasm

options.label: B
options.textMd: Net loss of water from the cell by osmosis

options.label: E
options.textMd: Rapid production of a second cell wall

explanationMd: The external solution has lower water potential, so water leaves through the selectively permeable membrane. The protoplast shrinks away from the rigid wall. This is plasmolysis, not destruction of the wall.

distractorRationale.a: Cytoplasm is not pumped out as a bulk fluid.
distractorRationale.e: A new wall would not explain shrinkage.
distractorRationale.c: The wall remains while the protoplast shrinks.
distractorRationale.d: Chloroplast displacement is not the cause of volume loss.
